summary: Indiana gives the practice real, citable leverage, but which law applies depends on the plan type, not the carrier brand. FULLY INSURED AND HMO (IC 27-8-5.7, IC 27-13-36.2): payers must flag claim defects within 30 days (electronic) or 45 days (paper), or the claim is legally clean; clean claims must be paid or denied in 30/45 days, and late payment owes interest from day 31/46 at the IC 12-15-21-3(7)(A) rate. That rate is 4% for 2026 as published by the Worker's Compensation Board, or 5% from the Comptroller's General Fund yields of 4.55% and 4.90%; IDOI has not issued a rate bulletin since 2019. Downcoding: since 2023 an insurer may not alter a CPT code on a clean claim unless coding rules or the contract allow it or someone reviewed the record (IC 27-8-5.7-6.5). From July 1, 2026 IC 27-1-52 requires CARC/RARC notice with clinical reasons, original and revised codes and amounts, an appeal window of at least 180 days, and batch appeals 'without restriction'. It bars AI-only medical-necessity downcodes. Recoupment: for current plan years overpayments and underpayment corrections are limited to 2 years from payment. For plan years beginning after December 31, 2026 under policies renewed after June 30, 2026: 180-day recoupment limit, 3-year audit limit, the practice's underpayment notice due within 180 days of payment, no retroactive CPT rate cuts, and 60 days notice of rate cuts. Prior authorization (also Medicaid MCEs and the state employee plan): authorized claims cannot be denied except for six listed reasons; intraoperative unanticipated services (Mohs repairs) cannot be denied for lack of authorization; a late authorization decision is deemed approved. DO THEY HAVE TO ANSWER? Yes. Grievances (patient-designated provider): acknowledge in 5 business days (3 for HMOs), resolve in 20 business days, appeals in 45 days; missing 45 days is itself an unfair practice. External review for medical-necessity denials binds the payer and the payer pays for it. An IDOI complaint (one per patient, claim of $250 or more, 90+ days late) triggers a required written response from the insurer within 20 business days (IC 27-4-1-5.6; IDOI guidelines). Unfair claim practices carry penalties up to $25,000 ($50,000 if knowing) per violation after hearing. There is no private right to sue under IC 27-4-1. Prompt-pay penalties are aggregate by calendar-year compliance percentage. MEDICAID MCEs (IC 12-15-13, 405 IAC 1-1.6, FSSA contracts): pay or deny in 21/30 days with interest from day 22/31; informal dispute within 60 days; formal appeal decided in 45 days or the claim is deemed approved. Binding AHLA arbitration can consolidate many claims, and the loser pays the costs. MCEs owe FSSA liquidated damages for slow claims and disputes. DOES NOT APPLY: self-funded ERISA plans (UMR, UHC Shared Services self-funded, UMWA Funds), Medicare, Medicare Advantage, VA CCN. The State of Indiana employee plan has its own prompt-pay law (IC 5-10-8.1). Letters should state these rights and concrete next steps truthfully. Indiana's intimidation statute covers threats to expose a party to disgrace or to falsely harm its reputation. The Indiana Code was read from the official 2026 files on iga.in.gov. 405 IAC was read via Cornell LII because the official IAR viewer could not be used here.

rules.quote: Failure of an insurer to notify a provider as required under subsection (b) establishes the submitted claim as a clean claim.
rules.applies_to: Fully insured accident and sickness policies issued in Indiana (IC 27-8-5.7-2, -3: insurance companies with an Indiana certificate of authority, their PPO plans, and administrators that adjust claims for those policies). Contracted and non-contracted providers alike. Not self-funded ERISA plans, not Medicare Advantage, not Medicaid managed care.
rules.requires: Insurer must tell the provider of any deficiency in a submitted claim, and describe the remedy needed to make it clean, within 30 days (electronic) or 45 days (paper). 'Clean claim' = 'no defect, impropriety, or particular circumstance requiring special treatment preventing payment.'
rules.deadline: 30 days after an electronic claim is received / 45 days after a paper claim is received (notice of deficiencies).
rules.consequence: If no deficiency notice is sent in time, the claim is legally a clean claim, so the 30/45-day pay-or-deny clock and statutory interest (IC 27-8-5.7-6) run.
rules.provider_use: For 'no answer' items: state the date received (837/277CA acknowledgment), that no deficiency notice was received within 30/45 days, and that the claim is therefore clean by operation of IC 27-8-5.7-5(c); demand payment plus interest. Keep the clearinghouse acceptance report as proof of receipt.

rules.quote: An insurer shall pay or deny each clean claim as follows: (1) If the claim is filed electronically, within thirty (30) days after the date the claim is received by the insurer.
rules.applies_to: Fully insured accident and sickness policies issued in Indiana (IC 27-8-5.7-2, -3: insurance companies with an Indiana certificate of authority, their PPO plans, and administrators that adjust claims for those policies). Contracted and non-contracted providers alike. Not self-funded ERISA plans, not Medicare Advantage, not Medicaid managed care.
rules.requires: Pay or deny each clean claim within 30 days (electronic) or 45 days (paper) after receipt. If the insurer misses the deadline and later pays, it must pay the provider interest on the policy allowable amount, accruing from day 31 (electronic) or day 46 (paper) after filing until the date paid, at the IC 12-15-21-3(7)(A) rate.
rules.deadline: 30 days (electronic) / 45 days (paper) from receipt; interest from day 31 / day 46 to payment date.
rules.consequence: Interest owed to the provider on the allowable amount (simple annual rate under IC 12-15-21-3(7)(A)); repeated failures count toward the aggregate civil penalty in IC 27-8-5.7-8 and IDOI administrative action.
rules.provider_use: Add a computed interest line to every late-paid Indiana fully insured claim (allowed x rate x days late/365). Interest is triggered only when the insurer neither paid nor denied in time; a timely denial later overturned does not trigger this statute's interest (reading of subsection (b)).

rules.quote: at a rate that is the percentage rounded to the nearest whole number that equals the average investment yield on state general fund money for the state's previous fiscal year, excluding pension fund investments, as published in the state comptroller's comprehensive annual financial report
rules.applies_to: All Indiana prompt-pay statutes (fully insured, HMO, Medicaid FFS and MCEs, state employee plan).
rules.requires: Interest is a whole-number annual rate from the Comptroller's ACFR. Published yields: FY2025 General Fund 4.90%, all funds except pension trust funds 4.65% (FY2025 ACFR); FY2024 General Fund 4.55%, all funds ex-pension 4.22% (FY2024 ACFR). The Indiana Worker's Compensation Board, which uses the same IC 12-15-21-3(7)(A) rate, publishes 'The rate of interest for 2026 shall be 4% annually'. IDOI's newest clean-claim rate bulletin is Bulletin 248 (April 10, 2019: 1% for 2019).
rules.deadline: Rate is annual; IDOI's past practice (Bulletin 248) applied the prior fiscal year's figure to the following calendar year.
rules.consequence: Determines the dollar amount of interest owed on late clean claims.
rules.provider_use: Demand interest 'at the rate required by IC 12-15-21-3(7)(A)'. If showing a number, 4% is the conservative published figure for 2026 (WCB); 5% follows the statute's General Fund wording with the FY2024 or FY2025 ACFR. Do not overstate: cite the formula, show the computation and the source year.

rules.quote: If the insurer has paid at least eighty-five percent (85%) but less than ninety-five percent (95%) of all clean claims received from all providers during the calendar year in compliance with this chapter, a civil penalty of up to ten thousand dollars ($10,000).
rules.applies_to: Fully insured accident and sickness policies issued in Indiana (IC 27-8-5.7-2, -3: insurance companies with an Indiana certificate of authority, their PPO plans, and administrators that adjust claims for those policies). Contracted and non-contracted providers alike. Not self-funded ERISA plans, not Medicare Advantage, not Medicaid managed care. The parallel HMO penalty is IC 27-13-36.2-6.
rules.requires: Insurers/HMOs must pay at least 95% of all clean claims in compliance with the chapter each calendar year.
rules.deadline: Measured per calendar year.
rules.consequence: Commissioner may assess aggregate penalties: 85-95% compliant up to $10,000; 60-85% $10,000-$100,000; under 60% $100,000-$200,000. Insurer may request an IC 4-21.5 hearing within 30 days. If imposed, no second penalty under IC 27-4-1 for the same activity.
rules.provider_use: This is a regulator penalty, not money to the practice. Use it by documenting a payer's late-payment rate from 835 data and submitting the pattern with IDOI complaints; letters can truthfully state that late clean claims are reportable to IDOI and count toward the IC 27-8-5.7-8 compliance percentage.

rules.quote: the health maintenance organization shall pay the provider that submitted the claim interest on the lesser of the usual, customary, and reasonable charge for the health care services provided to the enrollee or an amount agreed to
rules.applies_to: Indiana-licensed HMOs and limited service HMOs, and administrators adjusting claims for HMO contracts (IC 27-13-36.2-2). Contracted and non-contracted providers.
rules.requires: Same structure as IC 27-8-5.7: deficiency notice within 30/45 days or the claim is clean; pay or deny clean claims within 30/45 days; interest from day 31/46 until paid at the IC 12-15-21-3(7)(A) rate, computed on the lesser of UCR or the contracted amount.
rules.deadline: 30 days electronic / 45 days paper.
rules.consequence: Interest to the provider; aggregate civil penalties under IC 27-13-36.2-6; HMOs are also subject to IC 27-4-1 (IC 27-13-29-1(b)).
rules.provider_use: Identify whether the Indiana commercial product is an HMO contract; cite IC 27-13-36.2 instead of IC 27-8-5.7 for HMO members.

rules.quote: An insurer may not alter the CPT code submitted for a clean claim or pay for a CPT code of lesser monetary value unless:
rules.applies_to: Fully insured accident and sickness policies issued in Indiana (IC 27-8-5.7-2, -3: insurance companies with an Indiana certificate of authority, their PPO plans, and administrators that adjust claims for those policies). Contracted and non-contracted providers alike. Not self-funded ERISA plans, not Medicare Advantage, not Medicaid managed care. HMO parallel: IC 27-13-36.2-4.5.
rules.requires: No change to a submitted CPT code and no payment at a lower-value code on a clean claim unless (1) the submitted code is not in accordance with correct coding guidelines, clinical care guidelines, or the participating provider contract, or (2) the medical record was reviewed by an employee or contractor of the insurer. Insurer also may not pay only the codes needed for the final diagnosis when the billed codes were medically necessary to reach that diagnosis.
rules.deadline: No time limit stated; applies at adjudication.
rules.consequence: Violation of the prompt-pay chapter (reportable to IDOI); section 6.5(c) preserves the provider's appeal.
rules.provider_use: For E/M or procedure downcodes: demand identification of the coding guideline or contract term relied on, or of the employee/contractor who reviewed the medical record; if neither exists the alteration is not permitted. Useful for biopsy/excision codes paid at a lower-value code.

rules.quote: An insurer shall allow a provider to appeal in batches of similar claims involving substantially similar downcoding issues without restriction.
rules.applies_to: Insurers issuing accident and sickness policies, HMOs (basic health services), dental PPO plans, and any third party contractor of those entities (IC 27-1-52-6). Does NOT apply to the Medicaid program or Medicaid managed care organizations (IC 27-1-52-0.3).
rules.requires: (8) No downcoding that prevents a provider from billing and being paid for the actual service performed. (10) No downcoding based solely on the reported diagnosis code. (11) Every downcode must be reported with the appropriate CARC and RARC and must state the specific reason with reference to the clinical criteria used, the original and revised codes and payment amounts, and notice of appeal rights. (12) A clear appeal process with how-to notice, contact information for the individual managing the appeal, and an appeal window of not less than 180 days; batch appeals of similar claims allowed without restriction. (13) No targeted or discriminatory downcoding against providers who routinely treat complex or chronic conditions.
rules.deadline: Appeal window offered by the insurer must be at least 180 days. Effective July 1, 2026 (HEA 1271 SECTION 6).
rules.consequence: Statutory violation; IDOI must adopt rules (IC 27-1-52-14; none found yet). Enforcement is through IDOI.
rules.provider_use: Strongest Indiana tool for small-dollar downcodes: (a) appeal in batches, citing 27-1-52-12(b) if a payer insists on one claim per appeal; (b) flag any 835 downcode that lacks a CARC/RARC or the original-versus-revised code and amount as a 27-1-52-11 notice defect; (c) treat a payer appeal window shorter than 180 days as unlawful for Indiana fully insured/HMO members.

rules.quote: as the sole basis to downcode a claim based on medical necessity without the review of the covered individual's medical record by an employee or contractor of the insurer.
rules.applies_to: Same as IC 27-1-52 (insurers, HMOs, dental PPO plans, their contractors; not Medicaid). Subsection (b) applies to providers.
rules.requires: (a) An insurer may not use an automated process, system, or tool, including AI, as the sole basis to downcode on medical necessity without a human review of the medical record. (c) An insurer must disclose in an easily accessible and readable manner when AI is used to make an adverse prior authorization determination or to downcode a claim. (b) A provider may not use an automated process, system, or tool, including AI, to submit a health benefits claim without review by a provider or other person involved in developing the claim.
rules.deadline: Effective July 1, 2026.
rules.consequence: Statutory violation enforceable by IDOI. For the practice, subsection (b) is a compliance duty.
rules.provider_use: Ask in every downcode appeal whether AI or an automated tool was used and whether a person reviewed the record; absence of a record review is a defect. RemitWatch must keep a named human sign-off before any corrected or replacement claim it prepares is submitted for Indiana fully insured/HMO members.

rules.citation: IC 27-8-5.7-10 (text before the 2026 amendment, 2025 edition); IC 27-13-36.2-8 (same, HMO)
rules.quote: An insurer may not be required to correct a payment error to a provider more than two (2) years after the date on which a payment on a provider claim was made to the provider by the insurer.
rules.applies_to: Fully insured accident and sickness policies issued in Indiana (IC 27-8-5.7-2, -3: insurance companies with an Indiana certificate of authority, their PPO plans, and administrators that adjust claims for those policies). Contracted and non-contracted providers alike. Not self-funded ERISA plans, not Medicare Advantage, not Medicaid managed care. Governs claims under policies that are NOT issued, delivered, amended, or renewed after June 30, 2026 for plan years beginning after December 31, 2026 (the 2026 amendment's applicability clause, IC 27-8-5.7-0.5).
rules.requires: Insurer may not request repayment of, or offset, an overpayment more than 2 years after the overpayment; insurer is not required to correct a payment error (underpayment) more than 2 years after the payment. Fraud is excepted.
rules.deadline: 2 years from the payment date (both directions).
rules.consequence: Recoupment requests or offsets older than 2 years are barred; provider underpayment claims older than 2 years after payment cannot be forced.
rules.provider_use: Set RemitWatch's Indiana fully insured underpayment cutoff at 2 years after the payment date for 2026-and-earlier plan years; contest any takeback or offset of a payment more than 2 years old.

rules.quote: An insurer may not be required to correct a payment error to a provider if notice of the payment error is not provided within one hundred eighty (180) days after payment for a fully adjudicated claim is received.
rules.applies_to: Fully insured accident and sickness policies issued in Indiana (IC 27-8-5.7-2, -3: insurance companies with an Indiana certificate of authority, their PPO plans, and administrators that adjust claims for those policies). Contracted and non-contracted providers alike. Not self-funded ERISA plans, not Medicare Advantage, not Medicaid managed care. Only for claims under policies issued, delivered, amended, or renewed after June 30, 2026 AND providing coverage during a plan year beginning after December 31, 2026. Hospitals may agree to different time frames (subsection (f)).
rules.requires: Insurer may not request repayment of, or offset, an overpayment more than 180 days after it was made; may not recoup a paid claim more than 180 days after initial payment; may not retroactively audit a paid claim more than 3 years after initial payment. Provider must give notice of a payment error within 180 days after receiving payment. The fraud exception to subsections (a), (b) and (d) applies only when a court has made a final determination of fraud.
rules.deadline: 180 days after payment (recoupment and provider underpayment notice); 3 years (retroactive audit).
rules.consequence: Late recoupments are barred; underpayments not noticed within 180 days of payment cannot be forced on the insurer.
rules.provider_use: For 2027+ plan years, RemitWatch must send an underpayment notice within 180 days of the payment date for Indiana fully insured/HMO claims, even for cents-level variances; a dated fax is the notice record. Contest any recoupment of a claim paid more than 180 days earlier.

rules.quote: must be accompanied by an explanation of the reason for the adjustment, including:
rules.applies_to: Fully insured accident and sickness policies issued in Indiana (IC 27-8-5.7-2, -3: insurance companies with an Indiana certificate of authority, their PPO plans, and administrators that adjust claims for those policies). Contracted and non-contracted providers alike. Not self-funded ERISA plans, not Medicare Advantage, not Medicaid managed care. HMO parallel IC 27-13-36.2-9.
rules.requires: Any offset against a later claim must identify the claim on which the overpayment was made, the party financially responsible (if ascertainable), and the amount being taken through the adjusted claim.
rules.deadline: At the time of the offset.
rules.consequence: An offset without the required explanation violates the chapter (IDOI enforcement).
rules.provider_use: When an 835 shows a WO/FB/PLB offset without the source claim identified, demand the IC 27-8-5.7-11 explanation and reversal until provided.

rules.citation: IC 27-8-5.7-11.5; IC 27-13-36.2-9.5 (added by HEA 1271, applicability per -0.5 sections)
rules.quote: a provider may submit a claim to the appropriate insurer not later than ninety (90) days after the date the recoupment is made.
rules.applies_to: Fully insured accident and sickness policies issued in Indiana (IC 27-8-5.7-2, -3: insurance companies with an Indiana certificate of authority, their PPO plans, and administrators that adjust claims for those policies). Contracted and non-contracted providers alike. Not self-funded ERISA plans, not Medicare Advantage, not Medicaid managed care. Also applies to HMOs; claims under policies renewed after June 30, 2026 for plan years beginning after December 31, 2026.
rules.requires: When any insurer or HMO recoups for a coordination-of-benefits error, the provider may bill the correct insurer within 90 days after the recoupment, notwithstanding any other law, with documentation of the original submission and the recoupment.
rules.deadline: 90 days after the recoupment date.
rules.consequence: The correct insurer cannot deny that claim as untimely within the 90-day window.
rules.provider_use: Track COB recoupments as a trigger: bill the correct payer inside 90 days and attach the original claim proof and the recoupment remittance.

rules.citation: IC 27-8-5.7-6.7; IC 27-13-36.2-4.7 (added by HEA 1271; applicability per -0.5 sections)
rules.quote: An insurer may not retroactively reduce the reimbursement rate for any CPT code.
rules.applies_to: Fully insured accident and sickness policies issued in Indiana (IC 27-8-5.7-2, -3: insurance companies with an Indiana certificate of authority, their PPO plans, and administrators that adjust claims for those policies). Contracted and non-contracted providers alike. Not self-funded ERISA plans, not Medicare Advantage, not Medicaid managed care. Also applies to HMOs; claims under policies renewed after June 30, 2026 for plan years beginning after December 31, 2026.
rules.requires: No retroactive rate reductions for any CPT code; at least 60 days written notice by mail or email to the provider and posting on the insurer's website before a prospective rate reduction.
rules.deadline: 60 days advance notice for prospective reductions.
rules.consequence: A reduced rate applied retroactively, or without the 60-day notice, violates the statute.
rules.provider_use: When RemitWatch sees a payer's allowed amount for a CPT code drop below its own prior rate, ask for the 60-day notice and website posting; absent both, demand the prior rate.

rules.quote: An insurer may not deny a claim for reimbursement for a covered service or item provided to an insured on the sole basis that the referring provider is an out of network provider.
rules.applies_to: Fully insured accident and sickness policies issued in Indiana (IC 27-8-5.7-2, -3: insurance companies with an Indiana certificate of authority, their PPO plans, and administrators that adjust claims for those policies). Contracted and non-contracted providers alike. Not self-funded ERISA plans, not Medicare Advantage, not Medicaid managed care. Also applies to HMOs; policies/contracts issued, delivered, amended, or renewed after June 30, 2025.
rules.requires: No denial solely because the referring provider is out of network.
rules.deadline: Applies at adjudication.
rules.consequence: Such a denial is unlawful.
rules.provider_use: Pathology and Mohs referrals from out-of-network dermatologists or PCPs: cite this section against referral-based denials.

rules.quote: Failing to acknowledge and act reasonably promptly upon communications with respect to claims arising under insurance policies.
rules.applies_to: Insurers and (via IC 27-13-29-1(b)) Indiana HMOs. Not self-funded ERISA plans, Medicare Advantage, or Medicaid.
rules.requires: Unfair claim settlement practices include: not acknowledging and acting reasonably promptly on claim communications; no reasonable standards for prompt investigation; refusing to pay without a reasonable investigation; not affirming or denying coverage within a reasonable time; not attempting in good faith prompt, fair and equitable settlement when liability is reasonably clear; and (14) 'Failing to promptly provide a reasonable explanation of the basis in the insurance policy in relation to the facts or applicable law for denial of a claim'. Committing these 'with such frequency as to indicate a general practice' is an unfair practice under IC 27-4-1-4(a)(16).
rules.deadline: 'Reasonably prompt' / 'reasonable time' (no day count in the statute).
rules.consequence: Commissioner proceedings under IC 27-4-1-5 and -6 (see IN-UCSP-3).
rules.provider_use: Ask each payer for the specific policy provision and facts relied on for a denial (item 14) and document unanswered faxes (item 2). RemitWatch's records of unanswered appeals across many claims are the 'general practice' evidence.

rules.quote: Within twenty (20) business days from the date of receipt of the complaint, the insurer shall provide to the commissioner and the complaining party a written report
rules.applies_to: Any person who has submitted a claim to an insurer under an insurance policy (providers included) about an Indiana-regulated insurer or HMO.
rules.requires: If the commissioner believes an unfair claim settlement practice occurred, IDOI delivers the complaint to the insurer within 10 business days; the insurer must investigate and, within 20 business days of receipt, give IDOI and the complainant a written report of the specific reasons for its actions and inaction and, if unsettled, a good-faith estimate of the time to settle.
rules.deadline: IDOI: 10 business days; insurer: 20 business days from receipt of the complaint.
rules.consequence: An insurer that commits an unfair claims settlement practice or fails to comply with this section is subject to IC 27-4-1-6 action.
rules.provider_use: This is the legal answer to 'do they have to answer?': once IDOI forwards a complaint, the insurer must give the practice a written explanation within 20 business days.

rules.quote: Payment of a civil penalty of not more than twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) for each act or violation.
rules.applies_to: Insurers and HMOs found after an IC 4-21.5 hearing to have engaged in a practice defined in IC 27-4-1-4.
rules.requires: After hearing: cease and desist order; civil penalty up to $25,000 per act or violation, up to $50,000 if the person knew or reasonably should have known; suspension or revocation of license or certificate of authority if knowing. Violating a final cease and desist order: up to $25,000 per act (IC 27-4-1-12).
rules.deadline: None stated.
rules.consequence: Regulatory penalties payable to the state general fund. IC 27-4-1-18: 'This article does not create a cause of action' other than the commissioner's enforcement or an appeal of the commissioner's order, so the practice cannot sue under this chapter.
rules.provider_use: State accurately that unfair claim settlement practices are reportable to IDOI and carry penalties up to $25,000 per violation; do not claim a private right to sue under IC 27-4-1.

rules.citation: IDOI 'Guidelines for Providers Filing a Complaint with the Indiana Department of Insurance' and File a Provider Complaint page
rules.quote: The monetary amount on the claim must be $250 or more for healthcare providers claims, $5000 or more for hospital claims. Anything less will be sent back to the complainant.
rules.applies_to: Complaints against companies licensed in Indiana. IDOI states it has no jurisdiction over self-funded employer plans, Medicare, or Medicaid.
rules.requires: Provider or patient may file; first try to resolve with the insurer; IDOI assists when 'payment on the clean claim is more than 90 days late'; one complaint per patient ('complaints received that deal with more than one patient will be returned'); written cover letter with requested resolution, full legal name of insurer, card copy, policy and claim details; claim amount $250 or more. IDOI lists 'down-coding of claims without notice' and 'payment of non-network provider fee instead of usual and customary' as examples. Filing: online portal, fax 317-234-2103, or mail to Consumer Services Division, 311 W. Washington St., Suite 300, Indianapolis, IN 46204-2787.
rules.deadline: Claim must be more than 90 days late before IDOI assists; insurer has 20 business days to respond to IDOI.
rules.consequence: IDOI requests the insurer's explanation, suggests resolution, and takes administrative action when appropriate; IDOI 'cannot act as your collection service'.
rules.provider_use: Route Indiana fully insured/HMO claims of $250+ that are 90+ days unpaid to an IDOI complaint (one per patient). Sub-$250 items cannot go to IDOI individually; use batch appeals (IC 27-1-52-12(b)) and interest demands instead.

rules.quote: not later than forty-five (45) days after the appeal is filed. An insurer that violates this subsection commits an unfair and deceptive act or practice in the business of insurance under IC 27-4-1-4.
rules.applies_to: Insurers delivering accident and sickness policies in Indiana (IC 27-8-28-1, -9); excludes Medicare supplement, dental, vision, accident-only, long-term care and similar coverages (IC 27-8-28-1(b)). Grievance belongs to the covered individual; a provider may act as the designated representative.
rules.requires: Grievance includes dissatisfaction with 'the handling or payment of claims for health care services'. Filed orally or in writing; filed on the first date received. Acknowledge within 5 business days; resolve within 20 business days after receiving all information reasonably necessary (plus 10 business days with written notice of reason for delay); written resolution notice within 5 business days with reasons and appeal rights. Appeal: acknowledge within 5 business days; same-specialty panel for medical necessity/experimental issues; resolved not later than 45 days after filing; written decision within 5 business days with external review rights. Insurer may not act against a provider solely because it represents a covered individual in a grievance (-18).
rules.deadline: Ack 5 business days; grievance 20 business days (+10); appeal 45 days from filing.
rules.consequence: Missing the 45-day appeal deadline is itself an unfair and deceptive act (IC 27-4-1-4(a)(25)) and must be reported by the insurer to IDOI for that quarter (IC 27-8-28-17(d)).
rules.provider_use: With a signed patient designation, file payment disputes as a member grievance to start statutory clocks the insurer must meet; calendar day 45 of the appeal and cite IC 27-4-1-4(a)(25) when it passes.

rules.quote: an appeal must be resolved not later than forty-five (45) days after the appeal is filed.
rules.applies_to: Indiana-licensed HMOs and limited service HMOs, and administrators adjusting claims for HMO contracts (IC 27-13-36.2-2). Contracted and non-contracted providers. Grievance is a written complaint by or on behalf of the enrollee.
rules.requires: Acknowledge grievance within 3 business days; resolve within 20 business days after filing (plus 10 business days with written delay notice); written resolution within 5 business days after investigation. Appeal acknowledged within 3 business days; resolved within 45 days. HMO may not act against a provider solely for representing an enrollee (-11).
rules.deadline: Ack 3 business days; grievance 20 business days; appeal 45 days.
rules.consequence: Violating the 45-day appeal limit is an unfair and deceptive act under IC 27-4-1-4 (IC 27-13-10-8(c)) with quarterly reporting to IDOI.
rules.provider_use: Same as IN-GRV-1 for HMO members; use the shorter 3-business-day acknowledgment benchmark.

rules.quote: A determination made under section 15 of this chapter is binding on the insurer.
rules.applies_to: Insurers (IC 27-8-29) and HMOs (IC 27-13-10.1). Scope: adverse determinations of appropriateness or medical necessity, experimental/investigational determinations, and rescissions. Not available if the individual has a Medicare external review right (IC 27-8-29-23).
rules.requires: Covered individual or representative may request external review not more than 120 days after notice of the appeal resolution; insurer selects and rotates a certified IRO; IRO assigns a board-certified reviewer in the applicable specialty; standard decision within 15 business days, expedited within 72 hours; one external review per appeal resolution; insurer must cooperate and pays all IRO costs.
rules.deadline: Request within 120 days of the appeal decision; IRO decides in 15 business days (72 hours expedited).
rules.consequence: IRO decision binds the insurer/HMO; the covered individual pays nothing.
rules.provider_use: For medical-necessity denials (Mohs appropriateness, superficial radiation therapy called experimental, pathology add-ons), move to external review after the 45-day appeal: binding, free to the patient, decided by a board-certified specialist. Not useful for pure pricing or coding disputes.

rules.quote: The utilization review entity shall not deny the claim described in subsection (a) unless:
rules.applies_to: Utilization review entities (anyone performing prior authorization) for fully insured accident and sickness policies, HMOs, the State of Indiana self-insured employee plan (IC 5-10-8-19), and Indiana Medicaid risk-based managed care (IC 27-1-37.5-5; IC 12-15-12-0.9). Exclusions in IC 27-1-37.5-1: step-therapy exception procedures, local-unit public employer plans under IC 5-10-8-2.6, services provided under the PathWays for Aging and Health and Wellness Medicaid waivers, and anything preempted by federal Medicaid law. Self-funded ERISA plans are not covered as a practical matter (ERISA preemption). This section: prior authorization requested after June 30, 2025.
rules.requires: A claim for a service rendered in accordance with a prior authorization cannot be denied except for: knowing material misrepresentation with intent to deceive; service no longer covered on the date of service; provider no longer contracted; provider missed timely filing; the UR entity has no liability for the claim; or patient not covered on the date of service. Unintentional inconsistencies may be corrected and resubmitted.
rules.deadline: Applies to authorizations requested after June 30, 2025.
rules.consequence: Denial outside the listed reasons violates the chapter, which is an unfair or deceptive act (IC 27-1-37.5-15); a contrary contract term in contracts entered or renewed after June 30, 2025 is void (IC 27-1-37.5-14).
rules.provider_use: For any denial of an authorized Mohs, radiation, or surgical claim, attach the authorization and require the payer to identify which of the six statutory exceptions applies.

rules.quote: A utilization review entity may not: (1) require retrospective review of; or (2) deny a claim based solely on lack of prior authorization for; an unanticipated health care service
rules.applies_to: Utilization review entities (anyone performing prior authorization) for fully insured accident and sickness policies, HMOs, the State of Indiana self-insured employee plan (IC 5-10-8-19), and Indiana Medicaid risk-based managed care (IC 27-1-37.5-5; IC 12-15-12-0.9). Exclusions in IC 27-1-37.5-1: step-therapy exception procedures, local-unit public employer plans under IC 5-10-8-2.6, services provided under the PathWays for Aging and Health and Wellness Medicaid waivers, and anything preempted by federal Medicaid law. Self-funded ERISA plans are not covered as a practical matter (ERISA preemption). This section: claims filed after June 30, 2025.
rules.requires: A medically necessary service whose need was not anticipated when another service (authorized or not requiring authorization) was scheduled, and was determined at the time of that service, cannot be subjected to retrospective review or denied solely for lack of authorization; the provider must submit documentation explaining the medical necessity.
rules.deadline: Claims filed after June 30, 2025.
rules.consequence: Denial violates the chapter (IC 27-1-37.5-15 unfair practice).
rules.provider_use: Fits Mohs repairs and flap or graft closures decided intraoperatively after margins clear: send the operative note showing the defect size was unknown until surgery.

rules.quote: the health care service subject to prior authorization shall be automatically deemed authorized by the utilization review entity.
rules.applies_to: Utilization review entities (anyone performing prior authorization) for fully insured accident and sickness policies, HMOs, the State of Indiana self-insured employee plan (IC 5-10-8-19), and Indiana Medicaid risk-based managed care (IC 27-1-37.5-5; IC 12-15-12-0.9). Exclusions in IC 27-1-37.5-1: step-therapy exception procedures, local-unit public employer plans under IC 5-10-8-2.6, services provided under the PathWays for Aging and Health and Wellness Medicaid waivers, and anything preempted by federal Medicaid law. Self-funded ERISA plans are not covered as a practical matter (ERISA preemption). Sections 23 and 28 effective July 1, 2025 (SEA 480).
rules.requires: Prior authorization responses: urgent services within 24 hours; other services and drugs within 48 hours; weekends and state and federal holidays excluded. Adverse determinations must state specific reasons and suggested alternatives. If the UR entity fails to meet the chapter's deadlines or requirements, the service is automatically deemed authorized.
rules.deadline: 24 hours (urgent) / 48 hours (other), excluding weekends and holidays.
rules.consequence: Deemed authorization; IC 27-1-37.5-12 then limits denial of the claim.
rules.provider_use: Keep timestamped prior-authorization submission records; when the payer answered late, appeal any related denial as deemed authorized.

rules.quote: the failure to furnish proof within the time required under clause (A) or (B) does not invalidate or reduce any claim if it was not reasonably possible to furnish proof within that time
rules.applies_to: Group accident and sickness policies with an Indiana legal situs and individual policies delivered in Indiana. Provider contracts may set their own filing limits.
rules.requires: Policy must give 90 days after the loss for proof of loss; late proof is not invalid if it was not reasonably possible to furnish it sooner and it is furnished as soon as reasonably possible, but (except for legal incapacity) no later than 1 year after the proof was otherwise due. Claims filed by a provider must be paid in accordance with IC 27-8-5.7. No lawsuit on the policy sooner than 60 days after proof of loss or later than 3 years after proof was due.
rules.deadline: 90 days; extension up to 1 year when not reasonably possible; 3-year suit limit.
rules.consequence: An insurer cannot invalidate a late claim that meets the reasonably-possible standard within the outer limit.
rules.provider_use: For non-contracted claims denied as late, argue the policy's statutory proof-of-loss terms. No Indiana statute was found that sets a minimum timely-filing window for participating-provider contracts.

rules.quote: reimbursement payments under the contract shall be paid retroactive to the date the provider was provisionally credentialed.
rules.applies_to: Insurers that issue or administer policies covering basic health care services (IC 27-8-11-7(a)).
rules.requires: Deficiency notice on an unclean credentialing application within 5 business days; if no decision within 15 business days after a clean application, the insurer must provisionally credential the provider; once fully credentialed and contracted, pay retroactively to the provisional date.
rules.deadline: 5 business days (deficiency notice); 15 business days (decision).
rules.consequence: Retroactive payment at contract rates back to the provisional credentialing date.
rules.provider_use: For claims denied 'provider not credentialed' for new Indiana clinicians, show the clean application date and demand payment from the provisional date.

rules.quote: The administrator shall pay or deny each clean claim as follows:
rules.applies_to: Indiana state employee health plan: the state self-insurance program under IC 5-10-8-7(b), its contracted administrator, and prepaid plans under IC 5-10-8-7(c). A governmental plan, so ERISA preemption does not remove it.
rules.requires: Deficiency notice within 30/45 days or the claim is clean; pay or deny clean claims within 30 days (electronic) or 45 days (paper); interest from day 31/46 until paid on the plan allowable amount at the IC 12-15-21-3(7)(A) rate.
rules.deadline: 30 days electronic / 45 days paper.
rules.consequence: Interest owed to the provider.
rules.provider_use: Even though it is self-funded, cite IC 5-10-8.1 for State of Indiana employee plan members, whichever carrier administers it.

rules.quote: The compensation of a claim review agent for the performance of medical claims review may not be based on the amount by which claims are reduced for payment.
rules.applies_to: Third-party claim review agents and claim review consultants reviewing services delivered in Indiana for insurers, HMOs, or other benefit programs. Excludes Indiana-authorized insurers, HMOs, licensed administrators, and government agents.
rules.requires: Appropriateness determinations made by, or under standards approved by, a provider licensed in the same discipline; each determination states the principal reason; amount-charged determinations must disclose the factual basis, any claims database used (name and address), and any percentile limiter; appeals decided by a same-discipline provider within 30 days after all information is received; notice of appeal rights to the rendering provider; no compensation based on claim reductions.
rules.deadline: Appeal decision within 30 days after filing and complete information.
rules.consequence: IDOI enforcement; IDOI's fine schedule lists up to $5,000 for violations of the medical claims review agent law.
rules.provider_use: Could reach outside reviewers and repricers that cut Indiana claims; ask which database and percentile were used. Applying it to self-funded ERISA plans' vendors is unresolved (see open questions).

rules.quote: If the claim is filed electronically, within twenty-one (21) days after the date the claim is received by:
rules.applies_to: Indiana Medicaid: FSSA fee-for-service and every risk-based managed care entity under contract with OMPP (Hoosier Healthwise, HIP, Hoosier Care Connect, PathWays) and their subcontractors (IC 12-15-13-0.4). Excludes nursing facility claims.
rules.requires: 'Clean claim' = can be processed without more information from the provider or a third party (includes claims with state system errors; excludes claims under medical-necessity review or from providers under fraud investigation). Non-clean claims must be denied or suspended within 30 days with each reason stated. Clean claims must be paid or denied within 21 days (electronic) or 30 days (paper). Interest on the Medicaid allowable amount from day 22 (electronic) or day 31 (paper) until paid, at the IC 12-15-21-3(7)(A) rate.
rules.deadline: 21 days electronic / 30 days paper; non-clean claims 30 days.
rules.consequence: Interest owed to the provider; MCE contract liquidated damages (IN-MCD-2).
rules.provider_use: Shorter clocks than commercial: flag Indiana Medicaid MCE claims unpaid at day 22 (electronic) and demand statutory interest.

rules.citation: MHS HIP contract #69655, Exhibit 1 (HIP Scope of Work) sections 5.4, 8.5.1, 8.5.3 and Exhibit 2 'Claims Payment' and 'Provider Claim Disputes'; Humana PathWays contract #82035, Exhibit 1 sections 6.11.3, 9.7.3, 9.9.5
rules.quote: The Contractor shall pay interest on all clean claims paid late (i.e., in- or out-of- network claims) for which the Contractor is responsible
rules.applies_to: Indiana Medicaid MCEs under FSSA contracts (verified in the MHS HIP contract effective Jan 1, 2023 and the Humana PathWays contract commencing July 1, 2024; same template language expected in other MCE contracts but not verified).
rules.requires: Pay or deny clean electronic claims within 21 calendar days and paper within 30; interest at the IC 12-15-21-3(7)(A) rate on late clean claims, in or out of network; PathWays also requires interest on 'payments made inaccurately (paid upon the claim once adjudicated appropriately)' and denial of unclean claims within 30 days; MCEs must meet IC 27-13-36.2-3 deficiency-notice timelines. Disputes: resolve 99% of informal disputes within 30 calendar days and 99% of formal disputes within 45. PathWays: dispute decisions must explain facts and law ('Reference to general legal authorities alone is not acceptable') and overturned claims must be reprocessed with interest within 30 business days.
rules.deadline: 21/30 days for claims; 30/45 days for disputes; 30 business days to pay overturned disputes (PathWays).
rules.consequence: FSSA liquidated damages: $5,700 per deficient claim type when under 98% of clean claims are timely; $2,310 per quarter for missing the 99% dispute timeliness standards (HIP Exhibit 2).
rules.provider_use: Quote the MCE's own contract obligations in Medicaid disputes (state contract documents published by FSSA). For PathWays (60+ population, common for skin cancer), demand interest on corrected underpayments too.

rules.citation: 405 IAC 1-1.6-1, -2, -3, -5; HIP contract Exhibit 1 sections 5.4 and 8.5.1; PathWays contract section 6.11.3
rules.quote: the failure on the part of the panel shall have the effect of an approval by the panel of the provider's claim.
rules.applies_to: By rule, claims to Indiana Medicaid risk-based MCOs from non-contracted providers (405 IAC 1-1.6-1(a)); by FSSA contract, in-network providers too ('The Contractor's in-network provider claim dispute process must adhere to the same rules', HIP contract).
rules.requires: Informal stage: written objection within 60 days after receipt of written notice of the MCO's determination, or within 90 days of submission if the MCO made no determination within 30 days. Formal stage: if not resolved within 30 days after the informal process began, the provider has 60 days after the end of that 30-day period to file a written formal appeal; heard by a panel of uninvolved people knowledgeable in the policy, legal, and clinical issues, with the medical director consulting on medical necessity; provider may appear and be represented by an attorney or other representative; written determination within 45 days. A claim finally determined not to lack documentation must be processed within 30 days.
rules.deadline: Informal: 60 days from the determination notice (or 90 days from submission if no determination). Formal: within 60 days after day 30 of the informal stage. Panel decision: 45 days.
rules.consequence: If the panel does not decide within 45 days, the provider's claim is deemed approved (405 IAC 1-1.6-3(h)).
rules.provider_use: Calendar the formal appeal to the earlier of 60 days from the informal decision or day 90 after the informal objection; on day 46 of a formal appeal with no decision, demand payment as deemed approved under 405 IAC 1-1.6-3(h).

rules.quote: The fees and expenses of arbitration or other binding resolution procedure shall be borne by the nonprevailing party.
rules.applies_to: Same as IN-MCD-3 (non-contracted by rule; in-network through FSSA contract terms).
rules.requires: After the panel decision, the provider may take the matter to binding arbitration under the American Health Lawyers Association rules and the Indiana Uniform Arbitration Act (IC 34-57-2), unless the parties agree otherwise or a statute imposes another procedure. One arbitration may include matters from multiple formal claim procedures between the MCO and the provider. The nonprevailing party pays the fees and expenses.
rules.deadline: No filing deadline found in the rule (see open questions).
rules.consequence: Binding award; the losing party bears arbitration costs.
rules.provider_use: Bundle many small Medicaid MCE underpayments that lost at the panel into one arbitration; letters can state accurately that unresolved matters will be consolidated into binding AHLA arbitration with costs borne by the nonprevailing party.

rules.quote: a claim may not be denied because the claim does not comply with the void notice or bulletin
rules.applies_to: Indiana Medicaid: FSSA fee-for-service and every risk-based managed care entity under contract with OMPP (Hoosier Healthwise, HIP, Hoosier Care Connect, PathWays) and their subcontractors (IC 12-15-13-0.4).
rules.requires: A notice or bulletin by FSSA, its contractor, or an MCE changing prior authorization, claims processing, payment rates, or medical policies (where rulemaking is not required) cannot take effect until 30 days after it is communicated to affected parties; FSSA must provide it within 5 business days after its date.
rules.deadline: 30 days after communication.
rules.consequence: A non-compliant notice is void; claims may not be denied for not complying with it; it may not be reissued for 30 days unless federally required.
rules.provider_use: When an MCE denial rests on a new policy, ask for proof of the communication date; if under 30 days before the date of service, the denial is invalid.

rules.citation: HIP contract #69655 Exhibit 1 sections 5.4 and 8.5.1; PathWays contract #82035 sections 9.7.3 and 9.9.5; IHCP Claim Submission and Processing module, Section 11 (405 IAC 1-1-3)
rules.quote: the Contractor may pay a claim relating to the same services within six (6) months after the provider receives notice of the disposition of the Medicare claim.
rules.applies_to: Indiana Medicaid: FSSA fee-for-service and every risk-based managed care entity under contract with OMPP (Hoosier Healthwise, HIP, Hoosier Care Connect, PathWays) and their subcontractors (IC 12-15-13-0.4).
rules.requires: MCE in-network filing limit is set by the provider agreement and 'generally' 90 calendar days from service; out-of-network 180 days (HIP) or 6 months (PathWays). Waived automatically for retroactive eligibility and agency error; 90 days after a recoupment notice from a prior MCE, insurer, or FFS; PathWays: no timeliness denial when the delay came from determining third-party liability, and Medicare crossovers may be paid within 6 months after the Medicare disposition. FFS: 180 days from service; crossover claims with Medicare payment exempt; extensions for retroactive eligibility (1 year), retroactive PA, and delayed primary EOBs (180 days from EOB).
rules.deadline: Generally 90 days (in-network MCE), 180 days/6 months (out-of-network), 180 days (FFS); 6 months after Medicare disposition for PathWays crossovers.
rules.consequence: Late claims are denied unless an exception applies.
rules.provider_use: For Indiana Medicaid secondaries never billed behind Medicare, the 6-months-after-Medicare-disposition rule (PathWays) and the FFS crossover exemption may keep them collectible; check each MCE agreement for its in-network limit.

rules.citation: 405 IAC 1-1-3(c)-(e); IHCP Claim Administrative Review and Appeals module v7.1; 405 IAC 1-1.4; IC 4-21.5-3-7
rules.quote: Requests for administrative review must be filed within 60 calendar days of notification of claim payment or denial.
rules.applies_to: Indiana Medicaid fee-for-service (traditional Medicaid and carved-out services), not MCE claims.
rules.requires: Administrative review within 60 calendar days of the remittance date (portal secure correspondence, IHCP form, or letterhead letter); Gainwell confirms receipt within 10 business days and responds within 45 calendar days. Appeal of an adverse review within 15 calendar days of notice, with a statement of issues within 45 calendar days; heard by an OALP administrative law judge; objections to the ultimate authority within 15 days; then judicial review under IC 4-21.5-5.
rules.deadline: 60 days (review); 15 days (appeal); 45 days (statement of issues).
rules.consequence: Administrative review responses are appealable state agency actions.
rules.provider_use: Only for FFS Indiana Medicaid; MCE claims use the 405 IAC 1-1.6 process.

rules.quote: the law described in subsection (a) is controlling.
rules.applies_to: Indiana Medicaid managed care organizations.
rules.requires: Where an IC 27 insurance provision conflicts with administration of the Medicaid managed care program, Medicaid law (IC 12-15, IC 12-17.6, 42 CFR 438 and rules) controls, except the prior authorization chapter IC 27-1-37.5 after December 31, 2020. The downcoding chapter expressly excludes Medicaid and Medicaid MCOs.
rules.deadline: None.
rules.consequence: Do not cite IC 27-8-5.7, IC 27-1-52, or IC 27-4-1 against Medicaid MCEs; cite IC 12-15-13, 405 IAC 1-1.6, the FSSA contract, and IC 27-1-37.5.
rules.provider_use: RemitWatch's letter builder must switch citation sets by line of business, not by payer brand (the same carrier sells commercial, Medicaid, and MA).

rules.quote: (F) expose the person threatened to hatred, contempt, disgrace, or ridicule; (G) falsely harm the credit or business reputation of a person;
rules.applies_to: Anyone, including a medical practice and its software, communicating with a payer.
rules.requires: Communicating a 'threat' with intent that another person act against its will is intimidation; 'threat' includes an expressed intent to expose a person to hatred, contempt, disgrace, or ridicule, or to falsely harm its credit or business reputation.
rules.deadline: None.
rules.consequence: Criminal exposure for letters that threaten public shaming or false reputational harm to extract payment.
rules.provider_use: Leverage must be factual, lawful next steps: the statute violated, the interest owed, the date an IDOI complaint, grievance, external review, or arbitration will be filed, and the regulator's penalty range. Avoid threats of media exposure, public shaming, or claims the practice does not intend to carry out.

batch_and_channel: Batch appeals: IC 27-1-52-12(b) (effective July 1, 2026) requires insurers and HMOs to allow appeals 'in batches of similar claims involving substantially similar downcoding issues without restriction' (not Medicaid). This is the legal basis for bulk downcode appeals in one fax.

Consolidated arbitration: 405 IAC 1-1.6-4(b) lets one Medicaid MCE arbitration include matters from multiple formal claim procedures, and 4(c) puts fees and expenses on the nonprevailing party. Each claim must first finish the informal and formal stages.

IDOI complaints cannot be bulk: one patient per complaint, claim amount of $250 or more ($5,000 for hospitals), clean claim more than 90 days late, written cover letter stating the resolution sought. Online portal, fax 317-234-2103, or mail to Consumer Services Division, 311 W. Washington St., Suite 300, Indianapolis, IN 46204-2787 (IDOI guidelines). Pattern data from many claims can be attached as evidence of a 'general practice' (IC 27-4-1-4(a)(16)), but this was not confirmed with IDOI.

Grievances may be filed orally or in writing and count as filed on the first day received (IC 27-8-28-14). A faxed written grievance with a fax confirmation is the filing record. The provider needs the patient's designation as representative (IC 27-8-28-15(b), IC 27-13-10-6(b)).

Medicaid MCE disputes must be in writing: informal written objection (405 IAC 1-1.6-2(b)) and written formal appeal notice stating the basis (405 IAC 1-1.6-3(b)). Fax with confirmation works if the MCE accepts fax; check each MCE manual.

Indiana Medicaid FFS administrative review: IHCP Portal secure correspondence, the IHCP Claim Administrative Review Request form, or a letterhead letter marked 'Claim Administrative Review', to Gainwell Written Correspondence, PO Box 50442, Indianapolis, IN 46250-0418, within 60 days. Appeals go to FSSA OMPP (fax 317-232-4412) per the March 2026 module and BT202642.

Underpayment notices for 2027+ plan years must reach the insurer within 180 days after payment (IC 27-8-5.7-10(d) as amended). A dated batch fax listing each claim, the paid amount, and the expected amount is the cheapest way to preserve cents-level variances.

Interest demands cost almost nothing to add: one computed line per late clean claim (allowed amount x annual rate x days late / 365) under IC 27-8-5.7-6, IC 27-13-36.2-4, IC 12-15-13-1.7, or IC 5-10-8.1-7, as applicable.
Any corrected or replacement claims that RemitWatch prepares for Indiana fully insured or HMO members need human review before submission (IC 27-1-52-9(b)).
does_not_apply: Self-funded ERISA plans (UMR, UHC Shared Services self-funded groups, UMWA Health & Retirement Funds, most large employers): Indiana prompt pay, unfair claims, grievance/external review and downcoding statutes do not apply. IC 27-8-5.7-3 limits 'insurer' to companies issuing accident and sickness insurance policies; the ERISA deemer clause, 29 U.S.C. 1144(b)(2)(B), bars treating such plans as insurers; IDOI says it 'has no jurisdiction over self-funded employer group health plans'. Use ERISA/DOL claims rules instead (other research area).

Medicare Advantage (Humana MA, UHC MA, Anthem MA): 42 CFR 422.402 says MA standards 'supersede any State law or regulation (other than State licensing laws or State laws relating to plan solvency)'. IDOI also disclaims jurisdiction over Medicare. Indiana prompt pay, IC 27-1-52, and IDOI complaints are not available for MA claims.
Traditional Medicare (WPS J8 for Indiana) and VA Community Care Network (Optum): federal programs; Indiana insurance law does not govern them (VA CCN was not researched in detail here).

Indiana Medicaid MCEs: IC 27-1-52 excludes Medicaid (IC 27-1-52-0.3). IC 27 provisions yield to Medicaid law except the prior authorization chapter (IC 12-15-12-0.9). IDOI does not accept Medicaid complaints. Use IC 12-15-13, 405 IAC 1-1.6, and the FSSA contracts.

Grievance and external review chapters exclude Medicare supplement, dental, vision, accident-only, long-term care, disability income and similar coverages (IC 27-8-28-1(b)). External review covers medical necessity, appropriateness, experimental, and rescission only, not pricing or coding disputes. It is unavailable where a Medicare external review right exists (IC 27-8-29-23).
Unfair Claims Settlement Practices Act: no private right of action (IC 27-4-1-18); remedies run through IDOI.

Prompt-pay interest under IC 27-8-5.7-6 / IC 27-13-36.2-4 is triggered only when the payer failed to pay or deny a clean claim in time. A timely denial later reversed does not earn statutory interest (reading of subsection (b)). The PathWays contract is broader: it covers 'payments made inaccurately'.

The 2026 amendments (180-day recoupment and underpayment notice, 3-year audit, no retroactive CPT rate cuts with 60-day notice, 90-day COB refiling) apply only to claims under policies issued, delivered, amended, or renewed after June 30, 2026 that provide coverage in plan years beginning after December 31, 2026. Earlier plan years keep the 2-year rules.

405 IAC 1-1.6 by its own terms covers only providers not contracted with the MCO. In-network providers get the same process through FSSA contract language, which providers may not be able to enforce directly (not confirmed).
Kentucky law, ERISA claims procedure, Medicare and MA appeal rules are outside this Indiana area.
open_questions: Exact 2026 rate under IC 12-15-21-3(7)(A): the WCB publishes 4% for 2026, matching the FY2024 all-funds-ex-pension yield of 4.22%. The statute's 'state general fund money' wording gives 5% (FY2024 4.55%, FY2025 4.90%). No IDOI or FSSA notice newer than IDOI Bulletin 248 (2019, 1%) was found. Confirm with IDOI Legal (317-232-0143) before printing a number.
IDOI's '$250 or more' threshold: unclear whether it means the billed claim amount or the disputed balance; the form asks 'Amount of claim(s)'.
Whether IDOI will act on pattern evidence (many small claims) beyond single-patient complaints, e.g., toward IC 27-8-5.7-8 aggregate penalties or a market conduct review. Not found in IDOI materials.

Whether IC 27-8-5.7 prompt pay reaches Medicare supplement (Medigap) policies issued in Indiana. IC 27-8-5-1's definition has no Medigap exclusion, unlike IC 27-8-28-1(b), but no IDOI statement confirms it.

Deadline to demand arbitration after an MCE panel decision: 405 IAC 1-1.6-4 sets none; MCE provider manuals may. Current HIP/HHW/HCC MCE policy manuals are on a login-only FSSA site. AHLA arbitration fees were not checked.

Only two FSSA MCE contracts were read (MHS HIP #69655 without amendments, Humana PathWays #82035). Anthem, CareSource, UnitedHealthcare and Hoosier Care Connect/Healthwise contracts were not read and may differ.

405 IAC text was read via Cornell LII. The official Indiana Register/IAC viewer (iar.iga.in.gov) loads text from an API that was not usable in this session. Verify wording against the official IAC before quoting in letters.
IDOI has not yet adopted rules under IC 27-1-52-14 or issued a bulletin on HEA 1271 (none in the bulletin index through Bulletin 280, August 2026).
Whether IC 27-8-16 (claim review agents) can be enforced against repricing/claim-editing vendors serving self-funded ERISA plans, given ERISA preemption.

Formal-appeal timing conflict: 405 IAC 1-1.6-3(a) counts 60 days from the end of the 30-day informal period, while MCE materials describe 60 days from the informal decision. Calendar the earlier date.
No rule-based escalation route from an MCE to OMPP for unresolved claim disputes was found; an OMPP training deck mentions OMPPProviderRelations@fssa.IN.gov for eligibility denials only.
Whether participating-provider contracts may shorten the statutory proof-of-loss window in IC 27-8-5-19 / IC 27-8-5-3 for in-network claims (not researched; contract-specific).
